sections.normalized_html:
Symmetric data is characterized by values that occur with regular frequencies, forming a balanced, mirror-image shape around a central point.

In a symmetric distribution, the mean is equal to the center of the data set. Otherwise, the mean is found by dividing the sum of all data values by the number of values.

With this in mind, we proceed to calculate the mean for each data set.

  • Data set [MATH: G] is symmetric with [MATH: 5] values (an odd number), so its mean is the [MATH: 3]rd data value in the list: [MATH: \textrm{Mean}(G) = 58]

  • Data set [MATH: H] is not symmetric, so its mean is [MATH: Mean(H)|= (40 + 57 + 60 + 63 + y)/(5); = (220 + y)/(5).]

Since the mean of the data set [MATH: G] is the same as the mean of the data set [MATH: H,] we equate them and solve for [MATH: y{:}]

[MATH: Mean(H)|= Mean(G); (220 + y)/(5)|= 58; 220 + y|= 58 ⋅ 5; 220 + y|= 290; y|= 70]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: y] is [MATH: 70.]

items.title: Comparing a Dataset's Mean and Median

sections.normalized_html:
For which of the following data sets is the mean greater than the median?

  1. [MATH: 12,\: 12,\: 12,\: 12,\: 12,\: 12,\: 12]

  2. [MATH: 3,\: 6,\: 12,\: 24,\: 48,\: 96,\: 192]

  3. [MATH: 15,\: 25,\: 35,\: 45,\: 55,\: 65,\: 75]

  4. [MATH: 7,\: 17,\: 27,\: 37,\: 47,\: 57,\: 67]

Symmetric data is characterized by values that occur with regular frequencies, forming a balanced, mirror-image shape around a central point.

In a symmetric distribution, the mean and median are equal to the center of the data set. Otherwise, the mean is found by dividing the sum of all data values by the number of values, while the median is the middle value of the data set when the values are arranged in order from smallest to greatest.

With this in mind, we proceed to calculate the mean and median for each data set.

  • Data set I is symmetric with [MATH: 7] values (an odd number). Thus, the mean and median of this data set are the [MATH: 4]th element, which is equal to [MATH: 12.]

  • Data set II is not symmetric, so its mean is [MATH: Mean|= (3 + 6 + 12 + 24 + 48 + 96 + 192)/(7); ≈ 54.4.] On the other hand, since it contains [MATH: 7] ordered from smallest to greatest elements, its median is [MATH: \textrm{Median} = 24.] So, [MATH: \text{Mean}>\text{Median}.]

  • Data set III is symmetric with [MATH: 7] values (an odd number). Thus, the mean and median of this data set are the [MATH: 4]th element, which is equal to [MATH: 45.]

  • Data set IV is symmetric with [MATH: 7] values (an odd number). Thus, the mean and median of this data set are the [MATH: 4]th element, which is equal to [MATH: 37.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Item 2 — Example: Finding a Missing Value in a Dataset

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Symmetric data is characterized by values that occur with regular frequencies, forming a balanced, mirror-image shape around a central point.

In a symmetric distribution, the mean is equal to the center of the data set. Otherwise, the mean is found by dividing the sum of all data values by the number of values.

With this in mind, we proceed to calculate the mean for each data set.

- Data set [MATH: G] is symmetric with [MATH: 5] values (an odd number), so its mean is the [MATH: 3]rd data value in the list:
[MATH: \textrm{Mean}(G) = 58]
- Data set [MATH: H] is not symmetric, so its mean is
[MATH: Mean(H)|= (40 + 57 + 60 + 63 + y)/(5); = (220 + y)/(5).]

Since the mean of the data set [MATH: G] is the same as the mean of the data set [MATH: H,] we equate them and solve for [MATH: y{:}]

[MATH: Mean(H)|= Mean(G); (220 + y)/(5)|= 58; 220 + y|= 58 ⋅ 5; 220 + y|= 290; y|= 70]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: y] is [MATH: 70.]
